sources.citation: Connell, Bruce & David Zeitlyn. 2000. Njerep: A postcard from the edge. Studies in African Linguistics 29(1): 95-125. doi:10.32473/sal.v29i1.107370 (open at journals.flvc.org; note the FLVC OJS records for SAL 29(1) are cross-wired: record 107370, titled 'Observations on Kunama tone', serves the Njerep PDF; record 107369, titled 'Njerep..', serves the Kunama PDF).
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request); access check: open copy online (also online with a university library login)
sources.note: Nothing. Sec. 4 'Structural characteristics of Njerep' (pp. 103-107) covers 4.2 consonants, 4.3 vowels (7-vowel system), 4.4 Tones: 'Njerep has three level tones, High, Mid, and Low' with contours, 4.4.1 tone melodies (M possibly downstepped H but analysed as M), 4.4.2 complex (word-final falling) contours analysed as floating L morphemes. The words 'stress' and 'accent' do not occur anywhere in the article (text-layer a full-text search for stress/accent count 0); no statement on word-level prominence, rhythm or intonation.
